previous_turn_classification: progress: native font evidence demonstrated an explicit internal Encoding mapping
finding: read-fonts 0.39.2 returns code 43 as plus after malformed assignment syntax and after a later valid-shape assignment to a missing glyph name. A successful Type1Font parse and a resolved glyph id do not prove a complete source Encoding interpretation.

source_explanation.arithmetic-selector: The computed index is outside the supported Type1 literal assignment grammar. It must be rejected for exact source decoding, rather than ignored while retaining the preceding plus assignment.
source_explanation.missing-character: The later literal assignment names MissingGlyph, absent from CharStrings. The reader skips unresolved names and retains the earlier plus mapping. That stale name cannot establish Unicode for the final selector.
source_explanation.missing-put: The reader accepts an incomplete dup/index/name sequence without requiring put. This is not a certificate of a conforming assignment.

primary_reference.title: Adobe Type 1 Font Format
primary_reference.relevant_rule: Simplified parsers inspect top-level tokens; custom Encoding assignments use repeated dup/integer/name/put sequences terminated by def or readonly. Computed simple values do not conform.

library_source.finding: The sparse scanner skips unrelated tokens and invokes a callback for integer/name pairs without requiring dup or put. The callback updates only when a glyph name resolves, retaining any prior mapping otherwise. Encoding callers also discard the scanner result.

required_integration_contract: Use a complete top-level token validation of the supported Type1 declaration form; reject arithmetic, procedures, unsupported mutation and incomplete assignments rather than skip them.
Preserve the last declared selector name, including missing names; never keep an earlier Unicode value after a later unresolved assignment.
Verify referenced names against retained CharStrings and reuse the existing Adobe glyph-name conversion only after source validation.
Preserve explicit PDF Encoding and ToUnicode precedence, including explicitly unmapped ToUnicode entries.
Charge decoded embedded-program bytes together with ToUnicode and font identity work under existing aggregate extraction limits; keep malformed, unsupported and resource-limit results distinct.
Demonstrate the guard on the original source and all three counterexamples before real-panel adoption.
next_action: Implement or select a strict bounded Type1 declaration reader that can expose validation status and raw selector names. The general font library may still supply outline/name lookup after that check, but its current Encoding result alone must not be promoted to exact text.
